title: The Four Ways That Rise and the Eight That Descend
reading:
Through the complete circuit of states the soul passes through in its natural life, twelve ways open before it. Four of them are the ways of regeneration: chosen, reckoned among what is the Lord's, ascending toward life. By these the truth received within the soul is lifted up to its height, going forth out of the natural and being raised inward into conjunction. The doctrinal vessels that carry truth across the natural waters travel by these ways, and along them falsity is itself withdrawn — taken up, transmuted, and passed over into another condition where it can no longer hold the rational down.

The other eight ways are the ways of corruption. They draw the soul downward into the lowest state of the natural mind, where self-love has its root. They are the courses falsity takes when the proprium organizes the rational on its own terms, and they all run through the outer life of the flesh.

Hear what works through them. The first is lawlessness — the soul living as if no order from the Lord bound it, the natural mind multiplied in every form of disordered appetite. The second is the killing in every body: the act by which one love consumes another, the proprium destroying what does not serve it. The third is the wounding word — speech that strikes at the soul stretched in its purification, that injures the very work by which the rational is being raised, that strikes against truth as it suffers in the body of every soul still being made. And alongside these run the further ways of falsity: the speech that mocks what is holy, that derides the principles of the Lord as he goes forth toward the soul.

These are the eight downward courses. The four upward ways carry the soul into life; the eight downward ways pour out into the lowest state, where what cannot be raised is finally laid down.
